    Normed multiplicative bases and basic algebras #

    Definition 1.1 of the manuscript (main.tex): a basis 𝓑 of a finite-dimensional algebra A is multiplicative if bc ∈ 𝓑 ∪ {0} for all b, c ∈ 𝓑; it is normed if it contains a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents and 𝓑 ∩ (rad A)^n is a basis of (rad A)^n for every n ≥ 1.

    The algebra radical rad A is Mathlib's Jacobson radical Ring.jacobson A (the intersection of the maximal left ideals), regarded as a k-subspace. Its powers are products of k-subspaces, which agree with the ideal powers because rad A is a two-sided ideal.

                def MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.IsBasicAlgebra (A : Type v) [Ring A] :
                Prop

                A is basic: it has a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents whose principal right ideals e_i A are pairwise nonisomorphic. Here e_i A ≅ e_j A is expressed by elements x ∈ e_i A e_j, y ∈ e_j A e_i with xy = e_i and yx = e_j.
